title: Introduce hybrid quant-kernel stress runner and occupancy slab reporter
author: Ava Patel
description: Motivation: We need an automated harness that stresses mixed-precision and integer-backed kernels across sequence length distributions representative of production workloads. The goal is to (1) exercise quantized code paths (q4/q8/mixed) at varying batch/seq mixes, (2) surface per-kernel latency and memory regressions, and (3) export a compact occupancy-slab histogram that ties kernel hotness to slab allocation dynamics. This PR introduces two cooperating components: a) hybrid-quant-kernel-stress-runner: a reproducible workload runner that can spawn controlled surge patterns, probe kernel fallbacks, and record per-token breakdowns; b) occupancy-slab-reporter: a reporter that consumes runner traces and emits per-epoch slab occupancy histograms, per-kernel invocation counters, and a compact CSV summary for downstream dashboards. Description of changes (high level): - New runner binary under cmd/stress-runner that supports flags for --quant-mode (fp16|q4|q8|mixed), --seq-mix (json spec), --surge-interval, --concurrency, --kv-prefill-ratio and outputs protobuf traces + compressed trace tarball. - New reporter under tools/occupancy that ingests trace tarballs and emits: slab_occupancy_<epoch>.jsonl (newline-delimited), kernel_invocation_<epoch>.csv and a small per-run summary YAML. - Small additions to benchmark lab plumbing: CI job to run a smoke stress-runner with a toy model, a trace sanitizer utility to remove secrets and nondeterministic timestamps, and a kube job manifest example for running the harness in-cluster. Why this is different: Existing runners in the lab exercise sequence variety and batching logic, but none systematically target quantized kernel fidelity and the allocator slab dynamics that impact memory amplification and OOM-proneness when integer kernels thumbnail memory layout. Checklist: - [x] Implemented runner and reporter binaries - [x] Added unit tests for trace sanitizer and CSV exporter - [x] Added lightweight end-to-end smoke job in CI - [x] Added Linear tickets for follow-ups (ENG-1289, ENG-1342) - [x] Documented flags and output format in README under benchmark-lab/ops/README.md Usage notes: The runner supports a compact sequence-mix language: e.g. --seq-mix='[{"p":0.6,"len":32},{"p":0.3,"len":128},{"p":0.1,"len":512}]' and a quant-mode of "mixed" which will randomly choose q4/q8/fp16 kernels according to --quant-mix-probs. Example command used in internal experiments: ./stress-runner --quant-mode=mixed --quant-mix-probs='[0.5,0.3,0.2]' --seq-mix='[{"p":0.7,"len":64},{"p":0.3,"len":256}]' --concurrency=48 --surge-interval=120s. Key findings from local runs: - On a 16GB A100-like dev instance, mixed quant run (q4/q8/fp16) reduced total resident set by ~38% vs pure fp16 but exhibited a 10-14% p95 latency regression when sequence-length 256 portions spiked and triggered kernel fallbacks. - Occupancy slab reporter shows a long tail of 8KB slabs retained during q8-paths, indicating an allocator fragmentation pattern that amplifies peak RSS during surge tails. These are preliminary and captured in artifacts/bench-742018/2025-11-10/. Output artifacts: compressed traces, csvs, and a small flame snapshot (flamegraph.svg) are attached in CI artifacts for the smoke run. Backwards compat: Runner defaults to fp16 and reproduces existing bench harness behavior when quant-mode=fp16. Follow-ups (non-blocking): add automatic canary for kernel fallback threshold (ENG-1342), integrate CSV output into the perf dashboard, and extend reporter to emit a per-model CDF export for storage.
